item.description:
# FLOW 1.0.1274
- Adds FLOW support for native packages created by the owner-authenticated provider-media Import Edge. - Shows whether a provider package is awaiting a Brain match or has an associated Brain game, with access to supplied title and artwork. - Preserves provider identity and authored project content when an exact Brain association is added later.
This app update requires the matching Import Edge service for automatic SHIFTS package creation. Real receiver playback acceptance is tracked separately.

# FLOW 1.0.1269
- Export: one global clip-text style + crystal-clear, correctly-colored output

# FLOW 1.0.1265
- Export: attached NHL cascade child slices its own media, not the project video

# FLOW 1.0.1263
- Organizer attached-clip export, NHL dedupe, CI NAS gate

# FLOW 1.0.1258
- Folder auth, NHL auto-list, SELECT ALL, error detail, season pack

# FLOW 1.0.1241
- Container migration: merge into shared sidecar folders

# FLOW 1.0.1197
- ⌘K command palette with the Feature Map and the Highlights workflow: mark a selected video-lane clip with H, persist Highlights as a client-DB tag, and jump to live workflows from the palette. - Ghost shift handoff receipts now identify the FLOW service correctly, so Alumni/handoff packages no longer 409 on delivery. - FLOW Import Edge runtime works for either owner (Chris or Shane); the installer no longer ad-hoc signs and strips quarantine after install (FLOW-INST-01). - Accessibility fixes for the clip strip: per-clip targets, hosted clip AX walked via NSView, and the AX tree walk that could crash on CI removed. - Playback and library fixes: black-frame detection, IQ Library recenter, HANDEDNESS ordering, seek tolerance, container-local bookmarks, and font registration fallback. - BOB cockpit responses are structured and streaming updates are coalesced; NHL provider clocks are kept out of authored notes.

# FLOW 1.0.1113
- IQ Library clips no longer start with a black screen — the preview player's seek tolerance now matches the other playback paths. - Breakdown Export overlay text is smoother: all text sizes unified, raster supersampling raised to 3x, and the panel background is more solid during export. - NHL clip notes no longer carry SportsCode period-time stamps (e.g. "P2-18:42") that leaked from the database into the overlay and export. - Ghost shift import copies the .flowaipkg to ~/Desktop/FLOW/ with a canonical filename after completion.

# FLOW 1.0.1112
- IQ Library left panel now shows up to 48 relative metrics when typing (was capped at 10). - Clip multi-selection: Shift+click for range, Cmd+click to toggle, Cmd+A to select all visible. - Database load cached: processed clips and the parameter index are serialized to JSON so subsequent loads skip Realm conversion and index rebuild. - Breakdown Export overlay no longer shows prohibited auto-tags (GAME DATE, PERIOD, ASSISTS, CODE, GOAL SECONDS, etc.) that the live IQ Library overlay already hid. - IQ Library window opens on the display showing the main FLOW window instead of whichever screen has the cursor. - .flowaipkg files show the FLOW icon in Finder instead of a generic document icon.
